claims.text: The as-cast alloy has a homogeneous single-phase microstructure.
The as-cast alloy is chemically disordered.
A controlled annealing treatment can promote local chemical ordering and secondary-phase clusters.
An annealing window can produce nanoscale ordering without macroscopic phase separation.
HIP at 1230 °C and 152 MPa for 4 h induced a secondary HCP phase in initially BCC Ta20Nb20Hf20Zr20Ti20.
The proposed ordered clusters will be enriched in specific elemental combinations.
The proposed ordered clusters locally modify the phonon spectrum.
Induced short-range chemical ordering enhances local electron–phonon coupling.
Enhanced electron–phonon coupling in the ordered regions promotes Cooper-pair formation.
Cooper-pair formation in the ordered regions produces a measurable bulk superconducting state.
The fully disordered as-cast state should have a very low or absent superconducting transition because its electron–phonon interaction is insufficient.
Annealing will produce a sharper and possibly higher superconducting transition than in the as-cast material.
The annealed alloy will exhibit a resistivity drop to zero and an observable Meissner effect.
Secondary-phase content or degree of order will correlate with superconducting transition behavior.
The proposed effect applies to transition-metal compositions such as those containing Nb or Ti because ordering can modify their phonon spectra.
Extensive phase separation would be deleterious to the proposed superconductivity enhancement.
TEM and XRD will be used to compare ordering or secondary-phase formation in annealed and as-cast samples.
A lack of statistically significant superconducting-transition differences between the annealed and as-cast samples is specified as a falsifying result.
